title: Cohort-aware slow-roll and rollback playbook for model upgrades
creator: Maya Patel
description: Build an opinionated A/B/canary playbook and corresponding Console UX flows to safely validate model version splits with cohort-aware traffic control, sequential statistical checks, and automated rollback triggers. This ticket captures the product definition, success metrics, acceptance criteria, and handoff artifacts for Engineering to implement the runtime hooks and Console controls. Goal: reduce manual rollout overhead and reduce time-to-rollback when quality regressions are detected while preserving business throughput for low-risk cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Console: experiment wizard exposes cohort selection, initial split, step-up schedule, burn-in period, and a rollback policy editor
Runtime: traffic router supports cohort-scoped split percentages and shadowing with <100ms additional routing latency under normal load
Safety policy: default statistical checks (sequential p-value + Bayesian credible interval) evaluated every minute and can trigger automated rollback when thresholds met
Observability: predefined dashboard shows cohort-level metrics (p50/p95 latency, token cost, model quality metrics) and a time-series for the statistical test statistic
Runbook: on-call playbook with clear manual-rollback steps and incident tags auto-populated when automated rollback fires
tasks: Finalize experiment spec and default thresholds (PM)
Prototype Console wizard screens and copy (Design)
Implement cohort-aware routing and telemetry hooks (Eng: runtime & router)
Add sequential-test evaluator & rollback actuator (Eng: safety)
Create dashboards and alerts for canary runs (SRE/Observability)
Add E2E tests including low-traffic cohort shadowing and rollback backfill
statistical_spec: Primary strategy: sequential testing using a Wald-style sequential probability ratio test (SPRT) for binary quality flags (e.g., rejection rate) with alpha=0.05 and beta=0.2
Secondary/Bayesian: evaluate posterior of delta(helpfulness) with 95% credible interval; require ROPE exclusion (region of practical equivalence) before declaring regression
Minimum sample rules: per-cohort minimum N=500 requests in 24h or minimum 30 minutes of steady traffic for high-frequency cohorts
Early-stop rules: if both SPRT and Bayesian checks indicate harm OR absolute quality delta > 3% and sustained for 3 consecutive windows -> auto-rollback
Multiple comparisons: apply Holm-Bonferroni correction across cohorts for p-value thresholds to limit false positives
default_playbook_steps: 1) Create experiment in Console: name, canary version, baseline version
2) Define cohorts: global, paid-customers, region=EU, mobile-app-v2
3) Set initial split (default 5% per target cohort) and step-up schedule (5 -> 20 -> 50 over 24h windows) with burn-in (30m) between steps
4) Select metrics to monitor: quality flags, average score, latency p50/p95, cost/token
5) Attach statistical policy: SPRT + Bayesian ROPE (use defaults or custom thresholds), enable auto-rollback toggle
6) Start experiment and monitor dashboard; automatic notifications to #rollouts and on-call when thresholds crossed
7) If auto-rollback executes, a postmortem workflow is auto-created and owner is paged
rollback_triggers: auto: SPRT rejects null in favor of harm at alpha-adjusted threshold for >2 sequential windows
auto: Bayesian 95% posterior probability that delta < -0.02 (i.e., worse by >2%)
manual: SRE/PM escalates after observing unexplained increase in errors or latency beyond SLOs
safety: detection of policy violations (excessive toxic output) from safety webhook
risk_considerations: Cohort imbalance: small cohorts can produce noisy signals; enforce sample thresholds and apply more conservative decision rules
Metric drift: quality labels can shift over time; include periodic calibration and guardrails against stale reference sets
Data leakage: ensure evaluation telemetry excludes internal QA/test requests; add query param filtering and token-level tags
Rollback oscillation: add cool-down period of 2 hours after rollback before reattempting the same variant
